issues.title: Logger uses direct logging.getLogger
issues.description: The rule requires logger instances to be created using the pattern `logger: "logging.Logger" = get_logger("module_name")` but this code uses direct `logging.getLogger()` call without proper type annotation or using the standard get_logger utility
issues.rule_name: Logger Instances Must Follow Standard Initialization Pattern

issues.title: Advisory lock uses non-deterministic hash breaking concurrency control
issues.description: The advisory lock key generation uses Python's hash() function on the trigger ID string, which is non-deterministic across different Python processes due to hash randomization. This means different workers evaluating the same trigger will acquire different advisory locks, defeating the entire purpose of serializing concurrent evaluations. The original implementation correctly used int(trigger.id) to ensure all workers use the same lock key for a given trigger. This bug reintroduces the race condition that the PR was designed to fix, allowing multiple workers to fire the compound trigger concurrently.

issues.title: Race detection compares lengths instead of ID sets allowing double-firing
issues.description: The race detection logic compares only the count of deleted IDs rather than verifying the exact set of IDs match. This comparison using len(deleted_ids) != len(firing_ids) will incorrectly pass when a worker deletes the same number of firings but with different IDs than expected. For example, if firing_ids is {A, B} but deleted_ids is {C, D}, both have length 2 so the check passes and the trigger fires incorrectly. The correct implementation should use set equality (deleted_ids != firing_ids) to ensure the exact same firings were claimed, preventing spurious trigger firings when workers race.

issues.title: clear_child_firings returns wrong ID field breaking race detection
issues.description: The DELETE...RETURNING statement returns child_trigger_id instead of child_firing_id, causing a critical type mismatch in the race detection logic. The caller in triggers.py expects firing IDs (specific instances of firings) but receives trigger IDs (the template/definition). Since firing_ids contains UUIDs of specific firing instances while deleted_ids contains trigger template IDs, the comparison deleted_ids != firing_ids will always evaluate to true, causing the system to incorrectly believe it lost the race and skip all legitimate trigger firings. This breaks the entire compound trigger firing mechanism.

issues.title: Modified test file is in a non-mirroring directory structure
issues.description: Rule requires tests to mirror the source directory structure. The source module under test is `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py` (relative path `server/events/triggers.py`), but this PR adds/updates tests in `tests/events/server/triggers/test_composite_triggers.py`, which does not mirror the source path (it is `events/server/triggers/...` instead of `server/events/...`).

architecture.overview:
Composite triggers live in src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py. reactive_evaluation routes each incoming event to child EventTriggers, which emit a Firing. fire() dispatches to evaluate_composite_trigger when the parent is a CompositeTrigger. Child firings are persisted in the CompositeTriggerChildFiring table through helpers in composite_trigger_child_firing.py, which upsert one row per (automation, parent, child trigger). The parent fires once enough children are present, then calls act or recursively fires into a higher-level composite.

This PR inserts a pg_advisory_xact_lock before the upsert and read, so evaluations for the same parent serialize within a transaction. It also changes clear_child_firings to DELETE ... RETURNING and gates the fire on the number of rows claimed. Together these form a claim-then-fire protocol on top of the existing upsert.
steps: Entry point: triggers.reactive_evaluation(event) runs per event. Each child firing is upserted by upsert_child_firing, then evaluate_composite_trigger is called. The parent's num_expected_firings == 1 shortcut still fires immediately without the lock.

New lock: acquire_composite_trigger_lock runs only on PostgreSQL. It takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed on the parent trigger's ID. This PR computes that key with hash(str(trigger.id)), which is the part to check closely.

Lock ordering: the lock is taken after the shortcut and before clear_old_child_firings, upsert_child_firing, and get_child_firings. Reads after the lock see sibling firings that committed while this transaction waited.

Claim step: clear_child_firings now runs DELETE ... RETURNING child_trigger_id. The caller compares the returned count with len(firing_ids) and returns early on a mismatch. The return value and docstring disagree about whether IDs are child_firing_ids or child_trigger_ids.
Tests: a new TestCompoundTriggerConcurrency class uses asyncio.gather on two reactive_evaluation calls. Because the default test backend is SQLite, these tests exercise the non-locking path.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20106 - fix: resolve race condition in compound trigger evaluation
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR tries to fix two races in compound (composite) trigger evaluation. The first is a "never fires" race under READ COMMITTED, where two concurrent transactions each see only their own child firing. The fix takes a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock per parent trigger before upserting and reading child firings. The second is a "double fires" race, addressed by making clear_child_firings use DELETE ... RETURNING and skipping the fire when the delete does not claim every expected firing.

The design is sound. The lock sits inside the same transaction as the upsert and the subsequent read, so under READ COMMITTED the post-lock reads see committed sibling firings. The DELETE ... RETURNING claim is a reasonable second guard. However, the lock key is computed with Python's salted hash(), which differs between processes. Multiple server workers would therefore take different advisory locks for the same trigger, and the cross-worker race the PR targets would remain. The new regression tests also run on SQLite by default, where the lock is a no-op, so they cannot detect the race. There are smaller problems too: a return value that contradicts its docstring, and an unused import with a logger change.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The main fix does not work across processes. hash(str(trigger.id)) is randomized per interpreter by PYTHONHASHSEED, so the advisory lock only serializes within one process, and the never-firing race can still happen across server workers. The regression tests also pass without the fix on the default SQLite backend. These need to be fixed before merge. The rest is cleanup.

findings.title: Advisory lock key uses salted hash(), so it is not shared across processes
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/models/composite_trigger_child_firing.py`, `acquire_composite_trigger_lock` (around lines 39-42) computes `lock_key = hash(str(trigger.id)) % (2**63)`. Python's `hash()` is salted per process, so different server workers take different advisory locks for the same compound trigger and the race is not fixed across processes. Replace it with a deterministic derivation from the UUID, such as `trigger.id.int & (2**63 - 1)`, which fits a signed bigint. Update the comment to match. Keep the `pg_advisory_xact_lock` call and the SQLite no-op branch unchanged. Add a test that the key is stable and equals the expected value.

findings.title: New concurrency tests cannot detect the race on the default SQLite backend
findings.body:
The test suite's default database is SQLite (`tests/conftest.py` only switches to Postgres when a Postgres URL is configured). `acquire_composite_trigger_lock` is a no-op on SQLite, and `asyncio.gather` on SQLite serializes writes. These two tests therefore run the same code path as the base commit, so they would likely pass with the fix reverted. They give false confidence.

The two tests are also near-duplicates with the same events and the same assertions. The first test's docstring says it verifies the `DELETE ... RETURNING` fix, but nothing checks the return value or the skip branch.

::code{file="tests/events/server/triggers/test_composite_triggers.py" lines="1674-1711"}

What would make these meaningful:
- A deterministic test for the claim branch: monkeypatch `clear_child_firings` to return an empty or short set, then assert `act` is not called and the function returns. This covers the `len(deleted_ids) != len(firing_ids)` branch, which currently has no coverage.
- A direct test in `tests/events/server/models/test_composite_trigger_child_firing.py` that `clear_child_firings` returns the IDs it actually deleted. The existing `test_clear_child_firings` ignores the return value.
- For the lock, a test gated on Postgres (skip unless the backend is Postgres) that holds the lock in one session and verifies a second session blocks.
- Drop or merge the duplicate test.
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/events/server/triggers/test_composite_triggers.py`, the `TestCompoundTriggerConcurrency` tests (around lines 1674-1750) run on the default SQLite backend, where the advisory lock is a no-op, so they do not exercise the fix. The two tests are near-duplicates. Replace or augment them with deterministic tests: (1) monkeypatch `prefect.server.events.triggers.clear_child_firings` to return a short set and assert the parent is not fired (covers the skip branch in `evaluate_composite_trigger`); (2) in `tests/events/server/models/test_composite_trigger_child_firing.py`, assert that `clear_child_firings` returns the deleted IDs. Add a Postgres-only lock test that skips unless the backend is Postgres. Remove the duplicated test.

findings.title: clear_child_firings returns child_trigger_id but is documented and used as child_firing_id
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/models/composite_trigger_child_firing.py`, `clear_child_firings` (around lines 147-157) uses `.returning(...child_trigger_id)`, but its docstring and the PR description say it returns deleted `child_firing_id`s. Change the RETURNING column to `child_firing_id` and return `set(...)` of those. In `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py` (around line 396), change the `len(deleted_ids) != len(firing_ids)` check to a set comparison, `deleted_ids != firing_ids`, so the caller compares the same ID space. Keep the early return and the debug log, and update the log message to match.

findings.title: Logger switched to stdlib and get_logger import left unused
findings.body:
The `get_logger` import at line 27 is now unused, because the only remaining reference is the import itself. Linters will flag it (ruff F401). The logger was also changed from Prefect's `get_logger(__name__)` to `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, which drops the module's established convention and the `"logging.Logger"` annotation.

The `import logging` was also moved below the `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block, which reads oddly. None of this is needed for the fix, so the logger change should be reverted.

::diff{file="src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py" lines="66-73"}

Restore `logger: "logging.Logger" = get_logger(__name__)` and keep the original import placement. Remove the stdlib `logging` import unless it is still needed.

findings.title: Advisory lock placement is correct for the never-firing race
findings.body:
The lock is taken after the single-child shortcut and before `clear_old_child_firings`, `upsert_child_firing`, and `get_child_firings`. That places it in the same transaction as the upsert and the read. Under READ COMMITTED, a transaction that waits on the lock then sees the committed sibling firings in its read. The lock is transaction-scoped, so it releases on commit or rollback without manual cleanup.

::diff{file="src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py" lines="349-352"}

findings.title: DELETE ... RETURNING as a claim step is a sound second guard
findings.body:
Making the delete the claim is a good pattern. Only the worker whose delete actually removes the rows proceeds to fire, which closes the double-fire window even if the advisory lock were bypassed, for example on SQLite. Skipping quietly with a debug log, rather than raising, is the right behavior for a lost race.
